feed.title: NPR Topics: Business
feed.subtitle: Reporting on the money that flows through our economy, from Wall Street financial firms to Silicon Valley tech giants, small businesses, consumers, employers and workers. Plus podcast episodes of Planet Money and The Indicator.

entry.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
entry.summary: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high.

entry.title: The average cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. hits a record high: over $51,000
entry.summary: Vehicle transaction prices are up to a new record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book — and some buyers are extending their car loans to finance them.

entry.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
entry.summary: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement.

entry.title: Nvidia shares tumble as the company says it's investigating CEO Jensen Huang
entry.summary: Nvidia's share price falls after the company begins an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

entry.title: The business of El Niño
entry.summary: El Niño is expected to bring wild weather, but it's also business opportunity for some. Contractors are booked up as homeowners prepare for heavy rains and ski resorts gear up to cash in on snow.

entry.title: Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill?
entry.summary: Affordability concerns were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as tariffs and the war in Iran drove up prices, including food costs. Now, Americans are expecting relief from Washington.

entry.title: The Cybertruck's 'cause of death?' Insufficient demand
entry.summary: One of the most polarizing vehicles to hit the road will soon be a thing of history. Tesla will wind down manufacturing of its Cybertruck at the company's Gigafactory Texas mid-next year.

entry.title: This was the week the AI trade cracked. So what's next?
entry.summary: Big losses by AI shares in stock markets after Democrats won the midterm elections have left investors shaken and wondering comes next.

entry.title: Hiring jumps: The economy added 165,000 jobs last month
entry.summary: The U.S. job market improved last month, according to a report from the Labor Department Friday. Employers added more jobs than forecasters had expected and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.

entry.title: Why gold prices are surprisingly low
entry.summary: Gold tends to go up when there's uncertainty in the economy. For a while, the price reflected that. But this week, it dropped from a nearly $5,600 in January to below $4,000. What's going on?
